exercises.title: Trace: Backtracking Choose-Unchoose & Duplicate Sibling Pruning
exercises.objective: Trace `subsetsWithDup([1, 2, 2])` to verify why `i === start` allows the second `2` as a child (`[1, 2, 2]`) while `i > start` prunes it as a duplicate sibling (`[1, 2]`).
exercises.instructions: Follow `start`, loop index `i`, `path`, and the active recursion `callStack` at each decision point.
codeLines: for (let i = start; i < nums.length; i += 1) {

primaryVariant.label: Child Extension vs. Sibling Pruning on [1, 2, 2]
primaryVariant.edgeCaseNote: Watch `i = 2` be ACCEPTED when `start = 2` (child) and PRUNED when `start = 1` or `start = 0` (sibling).

steps.prompt: From `dfs(0)` we pick `i = 0 (1)`, from `dfs(1)` we pick `i = 1 (first 2)`, and enter `dfs(2)` with `path = [1, 2]`. At `i = 2` (`nums[2] = 2 === nums[1]`), why does line 7 allow `nums[2]` to be pushed?

stateSnapshot.annotation: At dfs(2), start = 2 and i = 2. Since i > start (2 > 2) is false, [1, 2, 2] is formed!

choices.label: Because i === start (2 === 2), so i > start is false: we are placing the second 2 into a new deeper slot to form [1, 2, 2]
choices.misconceptionFeedback: Correct! `i === start` means this is the very first candidate tested at depth `start = 2`.

choices.label: Because nums[2] !== nums[1]
choices.misconceptionFeedback: `nums[2]` and `nums[1]` are both `2`; it is `i > start` being `false` that permits it.

steps.correctExplanation: When `i === start`, we are extending `[1, 2]` to `[1, 2, 2]`, which is a unique 3-element subset.

steps.prompt: After `[1, 2, 2]` is recorded, `path.pop()` twice restores `path = [1]` back inside `dfs(1)` (`start = 1`). Now the loop in `dfs(1)` increments to `i = 2`. What happens at line 7?

stateSnapshot.annotation: In dfs(1), i > start (2 > 1) and nums[2] === nums[1] (2 === 2) -> continue!

choices.label: i > start (2 > 1) and nums[2] === nums[1] are both true, so continue skips i = 2 and prevents a duplicate [1, 2] subset
choices.misconceptionFeedback: Spot on! Choosing `nums[2]` into slot 2 right after unchoosing `nums[1]` from slot 2 would create a second `[1, 2]`.

choices.label: It pushes nums[2] to create [1, 2] a second time
choices.misconceptionFeedback: Line 7’s `continue` skips `path.push(nums[2])` when `i > start && nums[i] === nums[i - 1]`.

steps.correctExplanation: Sibling pruning skips `i = 2` at `start = 1`.

steps.prompt: Back in `dfs(0)` (`start = 0, path = []`), `i = 1` explores `[2]` and `[2, 2]` and pops back to `path = []`. When the root loop reaches `i = 2`, what happens?

stateSnapshot.annotation: At root start = 0, i = 2 has i > start (2 > 0) and nums[2] === nums[1] -> skipped!

choices.label: Skipped by continue (2 > 0 and nums[2] === nums[1]), returning all 6 unique subsets [[], [1], [1,2], [1,2,2], [2], [2,2]]
choices.misconceptionFeedback: Exact! The `i = 1` branch already generated all subsets starting with `2`.

choices.label: Explores [2] a second time at the root level
choices.misconceptionFeedback: At `start = 0, i = 2`, `i > start` is `2 > 0` (`true`), so the duplicate root branch is pruned.

steps.correctExplanation: All 6 unique subsets are returned with zero duplicate branches.

alternateVariant.label: All Identical Elements ([2, 2])
alternateVariant.edgeCaseNote: Shows how `[2, 2]` produces `[], [2], [2, 2]` (3 subsets instead of 4).

steps.prompt: At `dfs(0)`, `[]` is recorded. `i = 0` pushes `2`, `dfs(1)` records `[2]`, and inside `dfs(1)` `i = 1` (`i === start`) pushes `2` to record `[2, 2]`. After popping back to `dfs(0)` (`start = 0`), what happens at `i = 1`?

stateSnapshot.annotation: start = 0, i = 1: i > start (1 > 0) and nums[1] === nums[0] -> skipped.

choices.label: i = 1 has i > start (1 > 0) and nums[1] === nums[0], so it is skipped
choices.misconceptionFeedback: Correct! Only the first `2` is allowed to open a 1-element subset `[2]` from the root.

choices.label: i = 1 pushes 2 to form a second [2]
choices.misconceptionFeedback: Line 7 skips `i = 1` because `1 > 0 && 2 === 2`.

steps.correctExplanation: `i = 1` is pruned at `start = 0`.

steps.prompt: What is the final returned `res` array for `subsetsWithDup([2, 2])`?

stateSnapshot.annotation: Returns 3 unique subsets: [], [2], [2, 2].

choices.label: [[], [2], [2, 2]] (3 subsets corresponding to choosing 0, 1, or 2 copies of 2)
choices.misconceptionFeedback: Spot on! A multiset of `k` identical items has `k + 1` unique subsets.

choices.label: [[], [2], [2], [2, 2]] (4 subsets)
choices.misconceptionFeedback: The duplicate `[2]` was pruned at `start = 0, i = 1`.

edgeCaseCheck.question: What bug occurs if you forget `nums.sort((a, b) => a - b)` on `nums = [2, 1, 2]`?

choices.label: The two `2`s are separated by `1`, so `nums[i] === nums[i - 1]` is false and duplicate subsets like `[2]` and `[2, 1]`/`[1, 2]` are generated.
choices.misconceptionFeedback: Correct! Adjacent duplicate comparison `nums[i] === nums[i - 1]` relies completely on equal values sitting next to each other.

choices.label: The algorithm throws a RangeError.
choices.misconceptionFeedback: It runs without crashing, but fails to prune non-adjacent duplicates!

edgeCaseCheck.explanation: Sorting brings identical elements together in `O(n log n)` so duplicate check is `O(1)`.

exercises.title: Trace: Coin Change Bottom-Up Tabulation vs. Greedy Failure
exercises.objective: Trace bottom-up Coin Change on `coins = [1, 3, 4], amount = 6` to prove how `dp[a] = Math.min(dp[a], 1 + dp[a - c])` discovers the 2-coin optimum (`3 + 3`) where greedy (`4 + 1 + 1`) fails.
exercises.instructions: Inspect the `dp[0..6]` state table at each subproblem amount `a` and choose the exact transition.

primaryVariant.label: Non-Canonical Coins ([1, 3, 4] for amount = 6)
primaryVariant.edgeCaseNote: Greedy picks `4 + 1 + 1` (3 coins), whereas DP compares `1 + dp[6 - 3]` (`2` coins) against `1 + dp[6 - 4]` (`3` coins).

steps.prompt: With `dp[0] = 0`, we compute `dp[1] = 1` and `dp[2] = 2`. At `a = 3`, testing `c = 1` gives `1 + dp[2] = 3` and testing `c = 3` gives `1 + dp[0] = 1`. Why must `dp[0]` be initialized to `0`?

stateSnapshot.annotation: At a = 3, coin c = 3 reads 1 + dp[3 - 3] = 1 + dp[0] = 1 coin.

choices.label: Zero coins are needed to make amount 0, so any exact single-coin match a === c transitions to 1 + dp[0] = 1
choices.misconceptionFeedback: Correct! `dp[0] = 0` anchors every single-coin base transition `1 + dp[c - c] = 1`.

choices.label: dp[0] should be 1 because there is 1 way to make 0
choices.misconceptionFeedback: `1` is the base case for counting *combinations*, whereas here `dp[a]` stores minimum *coin count*.

steps.correctExplanation: `dp[0] = 0` makes every single coin `c` evaluate `dp[c] = 1 + dp[0] = 1`.

steps.prompt: At `a = 4`, coin `4` sets `dp[4] = 1 + dp[0] = 1`. Now at `a = 5`, what candidate values are compared across `coins = [1, 3, 4]`?

choices.label: c = 1 gives 1 + dp[4] = 2, c = 3 gives 1 + dp[2] = 3, and c = 4 gives 1 + dp[1] = 2, setting dp[5] = 2
choices.misconceptionFeedback: Spot on! Each coin `c` looks back `c` steps to an already-solved subproblem `dp[5 - c]`.

choices.label: dp[5] stays Infinity because 5 is not in coins
choices.misconceptionFeedback: Amount 5 is formed by combining one coin with a smaller solved remainder (`4 + 1` or `1 + 4`).

steps.correctExplanation: Comparing `2, 3, 2` sets `dp[5] = 2`.

steps.prompt: Finally at `a = 6`, we test `c = 1` (`1 + dp[5] = 3`), `c = 3` (`1 + dp[3] = 2`), and `c = 4` (`1 + dp[2] = 3`). How does DP beat the greedy `c = 4` choice?

stateSnapshot.annotation: At a = 6: c = 3 reads 1 + dp[3] = 2 (3 + 3), beating c = 4 which reads 1 + dp[2] = 3 (4 + 1 + 1)!

choices.label: c = 3 transitions from dp[3] = 1 to give 1 + 1 = 2 coins, beating c = 4 which transitions from dp[2] = 2 to give 3 coins
choices.misconceptionFeedback: Exact! Because `dp[3] = 1` and `dp[2] = 2` are already tabulated, `Math.min` picks `2` (`3 + 3`).

choices.label: The loop skips c = 4 because 6 is not divisible by 4
choices.misconceptionFeedback: The loop still tests `c = 4` (`1 + dp[2] = 3`), and `Math.min(2, 3)` retains `2`.

steps.correctExplanation: `dp[6] = 2` is returned.

alternateVariant.label: Unreachable Remainder (coins = [2], amount = 3)
alternateVariant.edgeCaseNote: Verifies how `Infinity` propagates for impossible odd amounts and turns into `-1` at line 11.

steps.prompt: With `coins = [2]`, `dp[0] = 0`, `dp[1] = Infinity`, and `dp[2] = 1 + dp[0] = 1`. At `a = 3`, what does `1 + dp[3 - 2]` evaluate to?

stateSnapshot.annotation: At a = 3, c = 2 reads 1 + dp[1] = 1 + Infinity = Infinity.

choices.label: 1 + dp[1] = 1 + Infinity = Infinity, so dp[3] remains Infinity
choices.misconceptionFeedback: Correct! In JavaScript, `1 + Infinity` is `Infinity`, cleanly propagating unreachability.

choices.label: dp[3] becomes 2
choices.misconceptionFeedback: `dp[1]` is `Infinity` (cannot make 1 with coin 2), not `1`.

steps.correctExplanation: `dp[3]` stays `Infinity`.

steps.prompt: At line 11, `dp[3]` is `Infinity`. What does `coinChange([2], 3)` return?

stateSnapshot.annotation: dp[3] === Infinity -> returns -1.

choices.label: Returns -1 because dp[amount] === Infinity
choices.misconceptionFeedback: Spot on! Line 11 converts the `Infinity` sentinel to `-1`.

choices.label: Returns Infinity
choices.misconceptionFeedback: The problem contract requires `-1` when the amount cannot be formed.

steps.correctExplanation: Line 11 returns `-1`.

edgeCaseCheck.question: What does `coinChange(coins, 0)` return when `amount = 0`?

choices.label: Returns `0` immediately because `dp[0] = 0` and the outer loop `for (let a = 1; a <= 0; ...)` does not run.
choices.misconceptionFeedback: Correct! Zero coins are needed to form amount 0.

choices.label: Returns `-1`.
choices.misconceptionFeedback: Amount 0 is always achievable using 0 coins.

edgeCaseCheck.explanation: `dp[0]` is initialized to `0`, which is not `Infinity`, so `0` is returned.

exercises.referenceInvariant: Before computing dp[a], every smaller amount 0 <= r < a holds its exact minimum coin count (or Infinity if unreachable).
exercises.hintText: Initialize `dp[0] = 0` and `dp[1..amount] = Infinity`, then take `Math.min(dp[a], 1 + dp[a - c])` for every coin `c <= a`.

practiceProblems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Direct application of the single-pass `minPrice` prefix invariant from Lesson 1.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Strictly decreasing prices `[7, 6, 4, 3, 1]` must return `0`, never a negative delta.

practiceProblems.title: Maximum Difference Between Increasing Elements
practiceProblems.pattern: Running Prefix Minimum with Strict Inequality
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Reinforces evaluating `nums[j] > minSoFar` strictly before updating `minSoFar`, returning `-1` when no strictly increasing pair exists.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Equal adjacent elements `[4, 4, 4]` must return `-1` because `nums[i] < nums[j]` is strictly required.

practiceProblems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Contrasts single-transaction prefix state with unlimited-transaction telescopic sum of positive adjacent steps.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Multi-day continuous rallies `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]` equal the sum of daily steps `(2-1)+(3-2)+(4-3)+(5-4) = 4`.

practiceProblems.title: Range Sum Query - Immutable
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Builds muscle memory for the `P[R + 1] - P[L]` padded prefix sum indexing invariant.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Queries starting at `left = 0` or spanning a single element `left === right`.

practiceProblems.title: Find Pivot Index
practiceProblems.pattern: Running Left Sum vs Total Minus Left Minus Current
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Practices maintaining exclusive left prefix sum `leftSum` against `totalSum - leftSum - nums[i]` in O(1) space.

practiceProblems.title: Product of Array Except Self
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: The signature benchmark for two-pass exclusive prefix and suffix state without division.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Arrays containing exactly one `0` vs. two or more `0`s.

practiceProblems.title: Move Zeroes

practiceProblems.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array II
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Tests comparing `nums[read]` against `nums[write - 2]` in the compacted prefix rather than `nums[read - 2]`.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Arrays of length `<= 2` and long runs of 4+ identical values.

practiceProblems.title: Maximum Subarray
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Directly applies the `Math.max(nums[i], currentEnd + nums[i])` subarray extension/reset invariant.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: All-negative arrays `[-5, -2, -9]` must return `-2`, not `0`.

practiceProblems.title: Rotate Array
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Reinforces O(1) space cyclic rearrangement via `k %= n` and three in-place reversals.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: `k >= nums.length` on a 1-element or 2-element array.

practiceProblems.title: Two Sum
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Foundational check for lookup-before-insert ordering and handling partner index `0`.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Duplicate numbers summing to target (`[3, 3]`, `target = 6`) and half-target self-collision (`[3, 2, 4]`, `target = 6`).

practiceProblems.title: Contains Duplicate
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Fast warm-up comparing early-exit Set insertion against full-array Set size.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Negative numbers and `0` repeated at the very end of the array.

practiceProblems.title: Contains Duplicate II
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Demonstrates when overwriting a key with its MOST RECENT index (`map.set(x, i)`) is required to minimize `i - prevIdx`.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: `k = 0` (must always return `false` since distinct indices have distance `>= 1`).

practiceProblems.title: Valid Anagram
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Practices checking length equality first, then verifying zero net frequency balance.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Strings of different lengths where one is a prefix of the other (`"ab"` vs `"aba"`).

practiceProblems.title: Group Anagrams
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Directly tests building collision-free `#`-delimited 26-slot frequency keys.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Words with `>= 10` occurrences of a single letter (`"bdddddddddd"` vs `"bbbbbbbbbbc"`).

practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Combines a frequency hash map with an `O(n)` frequency-indexed bucket array to avoid `O(n log n)` sorting.

practiceProblems.title: 3Sum Closest
practiceProblems.pattern: Sorted Anchor + Converging Pointers Minimizing `|sum - target|`
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Adapts the 3Sum two-pointer sweep to track minimum absolute delta while still moving `left`/`right` by signed comparison `sum < target`.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Exact hit `sum === target` allows immediate early return.

practiceProblems.title: Container With Most Water
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Directly applies the bottleneck proof from Lesson 3 and Exercise 8.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Equal heights `height[left] === height[right]` where inner walls are much taller.

practiceProblems.title: Trapping Rain Water
practiceProblems.pattern: Converging Pointers with Running `leftMax` and `rightMax` Bottleneck
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Extends bottleneck reasoning: whenever `leftMax <= rightMax`, water at `left` is determined solely by `leftMax - height[left]`.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Monotonically increasing or decreasing bars (or fewer than 3 bars) trap `0` water.

practiceProblems.title: Sort Colors
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Direct implementation of Lesson 4’s 4-region invariant in one pass and O(1) space.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Swapping `nums[mid] === 2` with `nums[high]` when `nums[high]` is `0` or `2` (do not increment `mid`!).

practiceProblems.title: Squares of a Sorted Array
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Shows that squaring a sorted array with negatives creates a V-shape whose largest values sit at the two ends, filling the output from `n - 1` down to `0`.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: All negative numbers `[-7, -3, -1]` where `left` always wins.

practiceProblems.title: Boats to Save People
practiceProblems.pattern: Greedy Heaviest + Lightest Pairing (`people[left] + people[right] <= limit`)
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Pairs the heaviest remaining person `right` with the lightest `left` if they fit together, otherwise puts `right` in their own boat.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Final remaining person when `left === right` (`while (left <= right)`).

practiceProblems.title: 4Sum
practiceProblems.pattern: Two Nested Duplicate-Safe Anchors + Converging Two Pointers
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Generalizes 3Sum’s duplicate-skipping invariant to `k = 4` (`i > 0` and `j > i + 1` duplicate guards).
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Large positive/negative values near `10^9` where `nums[i] === nums[i - 1]` must be checked per loop level (`j > i + 1`).

practiceProblems.title: Maximum Average Subarray I
practiceProblems.pattern: Fixed-Size Window O(1) Delta (`+= nums[i] - nums[i - k]`)
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Direct application of Lesson 1’s fixed-length rolling sum.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Single-window array of negative values (`[-1]`, `k = 1`) where `maxSum` must start at `windowSum`, not `0`.

practiceProblems.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
practiceProblems.pattern: Variable Window with `lastSeen` Index Map (`lastSeen.get(ch) >= left`)
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: The signature benchmark for Lesson 2 and Exercise 9.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: `"abba"` where stale index `0` for `"a"` lies to the left of `left = 2`.

practiceProblems.title: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
practiceProblems.pattern: Variable Window Shrinking While Valid (`while (sum >= target)`)
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Practices the shortest-valid-window variant where `best` is updated INSIDE the `while (windowSum >= target)` loop before shrinking `left`.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Total sum of entire array `< target`, which must return `0` (not `Infinity`).

practiceProblems.title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Directly applies Lesson 3 and Exercise 10.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: `k = 0` or `k >= s.length`.

practiceProblems.title: Permutation in String
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Combines Lesson 1’s fixed window size `s1.length` with Lesson 3’s O(1) frequency-match counter.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: `s1.length > s2.length`, which must immediately return `false`.

practiceProblems.title: Find All Anagrams in a String
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Collects every start index `left = right - p.length + 1` where the rolling window frequency matches `p`.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Overlapping anagrams such as `s = "abab", p = "ab"` returning `[0, 1, 2]`.

practiceProblems.title: Minimum Window Substring
practiceProblems.pattern: Variable Window with `formed === requiredDistinct` Threshold Counter
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Tests exact threshold counting (`windowCounts.get(ch) === targetCounts.get(ch)`) during expansion and contraction.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: `t` contains duplicate characters (`t = "AABC"`) or no valid window exists (`""`).

practiceProblems.title: Max Consecutive Ones III
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Cleanest binary-state variable window: increment `zeroCount` when `nums[right] === 0` and shrink `left` while `zeroCount > k`.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: `k = 0` on an array of all `0`s (`[0, 0, 0]` -> `0`).

practiceProblems.title: Fruit Into Baskets
practiceProblems.pattern: Longest Subarray with At Most 2 Distinct Values (`freq.size <= 2`)
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Translates a wordy story problem directly into "longest contiguous subarray with `freq.size <= 2`".
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Deleting a fruit type from `freq` (`freq.delete(x)`) only when its window count drops all the way to `0`.

practiceProblems.title: Subarrays with K Different Integers
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Direct application of Lesson 4’s `atMostKDistinct(nums, k) - atMostKDistinct(nums, k - 1)` identity.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: `k = 1` where `atMost(0)` must return `0`.

practiceProblems.title: Reverse Linked List
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Foundational drill for Lesson 2 and Exercise 11.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: `head = null` and 1-node list `1 -> null`.

practiceProblems.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Directly applies Lesson 1’s sentinel dummy node pattern.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: One or both input lists are `null`.

practiceProblems.title: Linked List Cycle
practiceProblems.pattern: Floyd Tortoise & Hare Collision Check (`slow === fast`)
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Verifies `while (fast !== null && fast.next !== null)` ordering and reference equality.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: 1-node list with no cycle vs 1-node self-cycle.

practiceProblems.title: Linked List Cycle II
practiceProblems.pattern: Two-Phase Floyd Cycle Entrance Finder (`finder = head`)
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Applies the Phase 2 pointer-reset proof from Lesson 3 to find the exact node where the cycle begins.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Cycle begins at `head` itself (`pos = 0`), so `finder === slow` is true before Phase 2 even steps.

practiceProblems.title: Middle of the Linked List
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Demonstrates that `while (fast !== null && fast.next !== null)` naturally lands `slow` on the second middle node for even-length lists.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: 2-node list `[1, 2]` returning node `2`.

practiceProblems.title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Combines a fixed-gap two-pointer runner with a `dummy` sentinel to handle deleting the head node (`n === length`).
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Deleting the only node in a 1-node list (`[1], n = 1` -> `null`).

practiceProblems.title: Reorder List
practiceProblems.pattern: Midpoint Split + Second-Half 3-Pointer Reversal + Alternating Zip
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Master synthesis problem combining Floyd midpoint, severing `slow.next = null`, 3-pointer reversal, and two-list interleaving.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Forgetting `slow.next = null` before reversing the second half creates a cycle.

practiceProblems.title: Copy List with Random Pointer
practiceProblems.pattern: Old-to-Clone Node Map (or Interleaved `A -> A'` Weaving)
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Tests mapping arbitrary node references (`random`) without duplicating nodes or failing on self-loops.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: `node.random === node` (self-pointing random pointer) and `head = null`.

practiceProblems.title: Add Two Numbers
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Practices `while (l1 !== null || l2 !== null || carry > 0)` with a dummy head.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Final carry after both lists end (`99 + 1 = 100`, requiring an extra tail node `1`).

practiceProblems.title: LRU Cache
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: The gold-standard systems + data-structure synthesis problem from Lesson 4.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Updating an existing key via `put(k, v)` when already at full capacity must NOT evict `tail.prev`.

practiceProblems.title: Valid Parentheses
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Direct application of Lesson 1’s opener stack and final `stack.length === 0` invariant.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Unclosed openers `"((("` or leading closer `")("`.

practiceProblems.title: Min Stack
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Practices snapshotting prefix minimums per stack frame so `getMin()` and `pop()` are O(1).
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Duplicate minimum values pushed and popped sequentially (`push(-2), push(-2), pop(), getMin()`).

practiceProblems.title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Reinforces popping `rightOperand` FIRST and `leftOperand` SECOND on non-commutative `/` and `-`.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Integer division truncation toward zero in JS (`Math.trunc(a / b)`, NOT `Math.floor(-6 / 132)`!).

practiceProblems.title: Daily Temperatures
practiceProblems.pattern: Monotonic Decreasing Stack of Waiting Indices
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: The canonical benchmark for Lesson 2 and Exercise 12.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Equal temperatures `[70, 70, 72]` must wait for strictly warmer `>`.

practiceProblems.title: Next Greater Element I
practiceProblems.pattern: Monotonic Decreasing Stack + Next-Greater Hash Map
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Combines a monotonic decreasing stack over `nums2` with a `Map` to answer subset queries from `nums1` in O(1).
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Elements in `nums2` that never see a greater element default to `-1`.

practiceProblems.title: Car Fleet
practiceProblems.pattern: Right-to-Left Arrival-Time Monotonic Stack (`time = (target - pos) / speed`)
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Shows how sorting cars by starting position descending and tracking arrival time `(target - pos) / speed` collapses catching-up cars.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Floating-point arrival time comparison (`curTime <= fleetLeadTime` merges into the ahead fleet).

practiceProblems.title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
practiceProblems.pattern: Monotonic Increasing Stack with Left & Right Span Boundaries
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Direct implementation of Lesson 3’s `width = i - leftBound - 1` span invariant and `0`-height sentinel flush.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Strictly increasing bars `[2, 4, 6]` where all bars are flushed at `i === heights.length`.

practiceProblems.title: Sliding Window Maximum
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Directly applies Lesson 4’s monotonic deque with `head` index expiration.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: `k = 1` and strictly decreasing arrays where front expiration `deque[head] <= i - k` does all the work.

practiceProblems.title: Decode String
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Practices pushing `(currentStr, currentNum)` on `[` and popping/repeating on `]`.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Multi-digit repeat counts (`"100[a]"`) and deeply nested brackets (`"3[a2[c]]"`).

practiceProblems.title: Asteroid Collision
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Tests a `while` collision loop where a left-moving asteroid (`< 0`) can destroy multiple smaller right-moving (`> 0`) stack tops, tie-annihilate, or be destroyed itself.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Left-moving asteroids followed by right-moving ones (`[-2, -1, 1, 2]`) NEVER collide because they move apart!

practiceProblems.title: Invert Binary Tree
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Clean warm-up for recursive tree mutation and base-case `null` handling.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Node with only one child (`left !== null, right === null`) must move that child to the opposite side.

practiceProblems.title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: The simplest bottom-up post-order recurrence.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: `root = null` returning `0`.

practiceProblems.title: Diameter of Binary Tree
practiceProblems.pattern: Post-Order Height Return + `leftH + rightH` Turning-Point Maximization
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Direct application of Lesson 1’s distinction between path turning at `node` vs branch ascending to parent.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Longest path does not pass through the global `root`.

practiceProblems.title: Balanced Binary Tree
practiceProblems.pattern: Bottom-Up Post-Order Height with `-1` Unbalanced Sentinel
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Proves how returning `-1` on `Math.abs(leftH - rightH) > 1` avoids `O(n^2)` top-down height re-computation.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Tree where the root’s left and right subtrees have equal max height, but an internal subtree is unbalanced.

practiceProblems.title: Same Tree
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Builds the lockstep two-tree comparison pattern (`isSameTree(p, q)`).
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Same values in different child positions (`[1, 2]` vs `[1, null, 2]`).

practiceProblems.title: Subtree of Another Tree
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Composes `isSameTree` across every candidate root in `root`.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: `root` contains a matching top pattern that has extra deeper descendants not present in `subRoot`.

practiceProblems.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Directly applies Lesson 3’s `O(h)` time, `O(1)` space BST split-point proof.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: One target node is the direct parent/ancestor of the other (`LCA(2, 4) = 2`).

practiceProblems.title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Direct implementation of Lesson 4 and Exercise 14.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: `root = null` returning `[]`.

practiceProblems.title: Binary Tree Right Side View
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Demonstrates why level-order BFS beats walking `node.right` when a left subtree extends deeper than the right subtree.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Left subtree is deeper than right subtree (`[1, 2, 3, 4]` -> `[1, 3, 4]`).

practiceProblems.title: Validate Binary Search Tree
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: The signature benchmark for Lesson 2 and Exercise 13.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Grandchild violating root bound (`[5, 4, 6, null, null, 3, 7]`) and duplicate values `[2, 2, 2]`.

practiceProblems.title: Kth Largest Element in a Stream
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Directly applies Lesson 2 and Exercise 15.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Initial `nums` array has length `k - 1` before the first `add(val)` call.

practiceProblems.title: Last Stone Weight
practiceProblems.pattern: Repeated Two-Max Pop & Difference Re-Insert on Max-Heap
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Clean drill for `popMax` twice and `pushMax(y - x)` when `y > x`.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: All stones annihilate completely (`[2, 2]`), requiring `0` to be returned when the heap is empty.

practiceProblems.title: K Closest Points to Origin
practiceProblems.pattern: Bounded Max-Heap of Size K by Squared Euclidean Distance (`x^2 + y^2`)
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Tests flipping to a Max-Heap of size `k` when keeping the `k` SMALLEST distances (and avoiding `Math.sqrt` via `x*x + y*y`).
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Tied distances and negative coordinates.

practiceProblems.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
practiceProblems.pattern: Size-K Min-Heap (`O(n log k)`) or 3-Way Quickselect
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Compares `O(n log k)` bounded Min-Heap against `O(n)` average 3-way Quickselect.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Heavy duplicate runs (where 2-way Quickselect degrades to `O(n^2)` but size-`k` Min-Heap stays `O(n log k)`).

practiceProblems.title: Task Scheduler
practiceProblems.pattern: Max-Heap of Remaining Frequencies + Cooldown Queue `(remainingCount, readyTime)`
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Coordinates a Max-Heap (always schedule most frequent available task) with a FIFO cooldown queue.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Heap becomes temporarily empty while tasks are still waiting in the cooldown queue (idle CPU cycles).

practiceProblems.title: Find Median from Data Stream
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Direct implementation of Lesson 4’s order and size balancing invariants.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Negative numbers and alternating odd/even stream lengths.

practiceProblems.title: Merge k Sorted Lists
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Direct benchmark for Lesson 3’s `O(N log k)` frontier merge.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: `lists = []` or `lists = [null, null]`.

practiceProblems.title: Reorganize String
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Pops the most frequent character, appends it, and holds it outside the heap for 1 step so the same character is never placed adjacently.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Max frequency `> Math.ceil(s.length / 2)` makes reorganization impossible (`return ""`).

practiceProblems.title: Kth Smallest Element in a Sorted Matrix
practiceProblems.pattern: K-Way Row Frontier Min-Heap `(val, r, c)`
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Treats the first column of up to `min(n, k)` rows as `k` sorted streams and pops `k` times.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: `k = 1` or `k = n * n`.

practiceProblems.title: Furthest Building You Can Reach
practiceProblems.pattern: Size-`L` Min-Heap of Ladder Climbs + Brick Deduction on Eviction
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Brilliant application of Lesson 2’s size-`k` Min-Heap: use ladders for the first `L` climbs, and whenever a new climb arrives, pay bricks for the SMALLEST climb `popMin(ladderClimbs)`!
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Downhill or flat steps (`heights[i + 1] <= heights[i]`) require 0 bricks and 0 ladders.

practiceProblems.title: Number of Islands
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Direct application of Lesson 1’s 4-directional grid flood-fill and visited sinking.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Grid of all `"1"`s (1 island) or all `"0"`s (0 islands).

practiceProblems.title: Max Area of Island
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Extends flood-fill DFS to return `1 + sum(4 neighbor areas)` for each connected component.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Grid with zero land cells must return `0`.

practiceProblems.title: Clone Graph
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Tests registering `map.set(node, clone)` BEFORE recursing on neighbors to avoid infinite cycle loops.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Null input graph (`node === null`) or single node with no neighbors.

practiceProblems.title: Rotting Oranges
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Directly implements Lesson 2’s simultaneous multi-source BFS wave and `fresh` counter.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Grid with `fresh === 0` initially (returns `0`) or an isolated fresh orange blocked by empty cells (returns `-1`).

practiceProblems.title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Applies reverse uphill traversal (`nextHeight >= currHeight`) from both ocean borders and intersects their visited sets.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Equal-height plateaus where water flows horizontally across flat neighbors.

practiceProblems.title: Course Schedule
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Tests Kahn’s zero-indegree queue or 3-color DFS cycle detection on prerequisite pairs.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Disconnected cycle (`1 <-> 2`) separate from a valid chain (`0 -> 3`).

practiceProblems.title: Course Schedule II
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Direct implementation of Exercise 16: emit vertices in Kahn queue order and return `[]` if `order.length < numCourses`.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Zero prerequisites (`prerequisites = []`) where `[0..numCourses-1]` is immediately valid.

practiceProblems.title: Redundant Connection
practiceProblems.pattern: Disjoint Set Union Cycle Edge Detection
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Directly applies Lesson 4’s Union-Find `find(u) === find(v)` cycle check.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: 1-indexed vertices `1..n` requiring `parent` array of length `n + 1`.

practiceProblems.title: Network Delay Time
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Practices Dijkstra edge relaxation `dist[u] + w < dist[v]` and returning `Math.max(...dist.slice(1))`.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Unreachable node leaving `dist[v] === Infinity` (must return `-1`).

practiceProblems.title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Contrasts standard Dijkstra with `K + 1` rounds of cloned-array Bellman-Ford relaxation.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: A longer-cost 1-stop path that unlocks a valid `<= K`-stop destination when a cheaper 3-stop path exceeds `K`.

practiceProblems.title: Subsets
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Foundational template for recording `[...path]` at every node and restoring `path.pop()` on return.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Always include the empty subset `[]` recorded at the root call `dfs(0)`.

practiceProblems.title: Subsets II
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Direct implementation of Lesson 3 and Exercise 17 (`nums.sort` + `if (i > start && nums[i] === nums[i - 1]) continue`).
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Unsorted input `[4, 4, 4, 1, 4]` which fails unless sorted numerically before `dfs(0)`.

practiceProblems.title: Permutations
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Contrasts `used[i]` full-range looping (`0..n-1`) against `start`-index subset loops.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Remembering to reset `used[i] = false` alongside `path.pop()` after each recursive call.

practiceProblems.title: Combination Sum
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Directly applies Lesson 2’s `dfs(i, rem - candidates[i])` self-index reuse without permutation duplicates.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Target smaller than all candidates returns `[]` cleanly via `rem < 0` pruning.

practiceProblems.title: Combination Sum II
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Combines single-use `dfs(i + 1)` progression with `i > start && candidates[i] === candidates[i - 1]` sibling pruning.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Input with many duplicate `1`s (`[1,1,1,1,1...]`) that TLEs without `i > start` pruning.

practiceProblems.title: Word Search
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Directly implements Lesson 4’s temporary `board[r][c] = "#"` marking and `board[r][c] = saved` restoration.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: 1x1 board `[["a"]]` with `word = "a"` where no neighbor step is needed.

practiceProblems.title: Palindrome Partitioning
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Practices pruning invalid prefix cuts `s[start..end]` before recursing on `end + 1`.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Single-character cuts are always palindromes, so every string has at least one partition.

practiceProblems.title: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Clean multi-way branching tree where depth `idx` iterates over letters mapped to `digits[idx]`.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Empty string `digits = ""` must return `[]`, NOT `[""]`.

practiceProblems.title: Generate Parentheses
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Demonstrates maintaining prefix validity invariants (`open < n` and `close < open`) during string generation.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Never branch on `")"` when `close === open`.

practiceProblems.title: N-Queens
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Capstone backtracking problem using `cols`, `diag1 (r - c)`, and `diag2 (r + c)` sets for O(1) pruning.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: `n = 2` or `n = 3` where zero valid board configurations exist (returns `[]`).

practiceProblems.title: Climbing Stairs
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Entry point for converting an `O(2^n)` recursive tree into an `O(n)` time, `O(1)` space rolling two-variable loop.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: `n = 1` returns `1` without entering a loop starting at `2`.

practiceProblems.title: House Robber
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Directly applies Lesson 1’s `curr = Math.max(prev1, prev2 + x)` transition.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: `[2, 1, 1, 2]` where the optimal choice skips two consecutive middle houses.

practiceProblems.title: House Robber II
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Reduces circular adjacency (`0` and `n - 1`) to `Math.max(robLinear(0..n-2), robLinear(1..n-1))`.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Single house `nums = [5]` where both `0..n-2` and `1..n-1` slices would be empty without a length-1 guard!

practiceProblems.title: Coin Change
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Direct implementation of Lesson 2 and Exercise 18 (`dp[a] = Math.min(dp[a], 1 + dp[a - c])`).
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: `amount = 0` (returns `0`) and unreachable amounts like `coins = [2], amount = 3` (returns `-1`).

practiceProblems.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Directly implements Lesson 3’s `dp[i] = Math.max(dp[i], dp[j] + 1)` over `j < i` with `nums[j] < nums[i]`.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Longest subsequence ending before the last element (`[1, 3, 6, 7, 9, 4, 10, 5, 6]`), requiring `Math.max(...dp)`.

practiceProblems.title: Word Break
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Applies prefix split transitions `dp[i] = dp[j] && wordSet.has(s.slice(j, i))` with `dp[0] = true`.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Overlapping dictionary prefixes like `s = "aaaaaaa", wordDict = ["aaaa", "aaa"]` where greedy matching fails.

practiceProblems.title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Tests Lesson 2’s backward inner loop `for (let s = target; s >= num; s--)` so each number is used at most once.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Odd total sum (`totalSum % 2 !== 0`) must return `false` immediately.

practiceProblems.title: Unique Paths
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Clean introduction to 2D grid transitions `dp[r][c] = dp[r - 1][c] + dp[r][c - 1]` and 1D row rolling compression.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: `m = 1` or `n = 1` single-row/single-column grid has exactly `1` path.

practiceProblems.title: Longest Common Subsequence
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Directly implements Lesson 4’s `(m + 1) x (n + 1)` matrix with diagonal match `1 + dp[i - 1][j - 1]`.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: Repeated characters like `"bsbininm"` and `"jmjkbkjkv"` where diagonal transition prevents double-counting.

practiceProblems.title: Edit Distance
practiceProblems.whyRecommended: Capstone 2D alignment problem combining base-row/column deletion/insertion costs with 3-way edit transitions.
practiceProblems.keyEdgeCase: One or both strings empty (`word1 = ""`), handled by `dp[i][0] = i` and `dp[0][j] = j` base borders.
